exposure: special risk factors (diabetes mellitus, gestational diabetes)
cohort: The study included a retrospective cohort of 16,092 women with singleton pregnancies giving birth between 2017 and 2022, with a subset of 4,603 mother-child pairs of liveborn, singleton full-term newborns used for detailed factor analysis.
finding: The rates of ever breastfeeding and exclusive breastfeeding at the breast significantly decreased between 2017 and 2022, and were lower in women with higher BMI, those undergoing cesarean section, and those delivering at 38 weeks compared to 40 weeks.
mod_finding: Exclusive breastfeeding at the breast was significantly lower in women undergoing a cesarean section (62.3%) compared to those with vaginal births (78.1%).
gest_age: The study included full-term newborns for factor analysis, and compared outcomes for deliveries at 38 weeks vs. 40 weeks of gestation.
